To draw a regular pentagon of side $30\text{ mm}$ using the general method (or arc intersection method):

1. Draw a horizontal base line $AB = 30\text{ mm}$.
2. At point $B$, construct an angle of $108^	ext{o}$ (since the interior angle of a regular pentagon is $\frac{(5-2)\times 180^	ext{o}}{5} = 108^	ext{o}$) and draw a line $BC = 30\text{ mm}$.
3. Alternatively, using compasses: With center $A$ and radius $30\text{ mm}$, draw an arc. With center $B$ and radius $30\text{ mm}$, draw another arc intersecting the first at a construction point.
4. Continue intersecting arcs with radius $30\text{ mm}$ from the newly found vertices until all five vertices ($A, B, C, D, E$) are located.
5. Join the vertices $A-B-C-D-E-A$ with continuous thick dark lines to complete the regular pentagon.
proTip: Remember that the interior angle formula for a regular polygon of $n$ sides is $\frac{(n-2) \times 180^\circ}{n}$. For a pentagon, it is $108^\circ$.
